items.title: 4.3.4 Combining List and Stack to Perform Sequential Operations (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of combining a list and a stack (PDF 121-122).

blocks.text: Lists aur stacks basic (bunyadi) data structures hain jo mil kar data ko ek controlled order (tay ki hui tarteeb) mein sambhalne ka powerful (taqatwar) tareeqa dete hain. List data ko flexible (lachak wale) tareeqe se rakhti aur us tak pohanch deti hai, jabke stack Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) order lagata hai; is liye yeh un kaamon mein useful hai jahan sab se taaza element pehle process karna ho.
Misal: numbers ki list ka order stack se ulta karna hai. Yeh list lein:
Is list ko stack se ulatne ke qadam:

items: Qadam 1: list ka har element stack par push karein. Sab push hone ke baad stack: [10 20 30 40 50] (50 top par).
Qadam 2: stack se elements ek ek kar ke pop karein aur wapas list mein dalein. Stack LIFO hai, is liye pehle 50, phir 40 ... nikalte hain, yaani ulta order.
Qadam 3: saare elements pop ho kar list mein aa jayen to list yeh ban jati hai:

blocks.text: Is misal mein stack list ke elements ko thori der ke liye rakhta hai, aur us ki LIFO aadat se order ulat jata hai. List aur stack mil kar ulatne (reversing), undo aur backtracking jaise kaam aasani se karte hain, jo bohat se algorithms aur applications mein aam hain.

numbers = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
stack = []
for n in numbers:
    stack.append(n)          # push
numbers = []
while stack:
    numbers.append(stack.pop())    # pop back into the list
print(numbers)    # [50, 40, 30, 20, 10]
blocks.caption: Yahi kaam Python mein (kitab mein code nahi; yeh hamara code hai)

blocks.prompt: Do aur kaam bataiye jin mein list aur stack mil kar kaam karte hain.
blocks.explanation: Undo (document ki states (halat) ki list aur taaza actions ka stack) aur backtracking (options ki list aur ab tak try kiye gaye raaste ka stack).

items: List aur stack: sab push, phir sab pop, aur order ulat: [50, 40, 30, 20, 10].
